search_bias: evaluation/verifiers; finite policy-game duality; least-favorable fixed latent map priors; numerical optimality-gap certificates for anytime-valid hard-deadline paired-sign tests

finite_policy_zero_sum_game.construction: Take a library of valid hard-deadline paired-sign policies indexed by prespecified Bellman design pairs (q_design_low,q_design_high). Build payoff matrix A[j,m]=Pr_m(policy j rejects by deadline) for fixed latent maps m in {correct,flat,inverted}. Solve max_w min_m sum_j w_j A[j,m] over a protocol-fixed ex-ante randomized mixture w. The finite-game dual is min_p max_j sum_m p_m A[j,m] over a prior p on latent maps. This gives a library-relative least-favorable prior and a saddle certificate without pretending the library is the full policy space.
finite_policy_zero_sum_game.validity: Each component policy is a predictable affine e-process. Selecting one component by randomness fixed before any paired outcomes preserves the same alpha-level anytime-valid guarantee. Outcome-adaptive choice of the component would require separate correction and is not used here.
finite_policy_zero_sum_game.scope_guard: The game value is exact only for the finite numerical policy library/payoff matrix. The map-specific inverted optimum remains a universal upper bound on the full maximin value within the underlying discretized Bellman model.

T50_library_saddle.library_result: The finite-game solution is degenerate: weight 1 on design (.80,.60), value .4086945, matching the inverted-map Bellman upper bound at the same grid resolution.
T50_library_saddle.interpretation: This independently recovers the predecessor saddle argument: no randomization or latent-map learning is needed at T=50 for this discretized map set.

T100_refined_policy_game.library: 45 high-resolution design pairs with q_low in .785:.0025:.805 and q_high in .595:.0025:.605; Bellman wealth/action grids 800/181.
T100_refined_policy_game.interpretation: The least-favorable prior is nearly degenerate on inverted but puts about 1.14% mass on correct; flat is slack. The randomized policy equalizes correct and inverted power while flat stays above. Any richer history-dependent or belief-state policy can improve worst-case power by at most about 0.0061 percentage point relative to this library saddle, modulo the numerical-grid approximation.

T200_refined_policy_game.library: 45 design pairs with q_low .74:.01:.82 and q_high .595:.005:.615; Bellman wealth/action grids 650/141.
T200_refined_policy_game.interpretation: By T=200 the least-favorable prior in the searched game shifts more mass toward correct (~4.55%), reflecting that a policy over-specialized to the inverted transfer can make correct the binding state. Flat remains non-binding. The full-policy learning headroom is still bounded to roughly 0.055 percentage point by the inverted-map optimum.

horizon_dependent_least_favorable_suppor.observed_pattern: T=20/T=50: degenerate inverted state is binding. T=100: finite-game dual uses about 1.14% correct and 98.86% inverted. T=200: about 4.55% correct and 95.45% inverted. Flat receives zero dual mass in the refined T=100/T=200 libraries.
horizon_dependent_least_favorable_suppor.measurement_implication: A robust evaluator should not hard-code one least-favorable prior across budgets. The environment that limits finite-horizon resolution can change with the decision horizon even when the physical map set is unchanged.

belief_learning_headroom_bound.derivation: For any unrestricted policy, worst-map power <= V*_inverted because inverted is one admissible latent map. Once a concrete policy or valid ex-ante policy mixture reaches v, every richer mechanism including posterior learning over the latent map can improve worst-case deadline power by at most V*_inverted-v.
belief_learning_headroom_bound.interpretation: In this stylized problem, preserving the cross-stratum coupling captures almost all of the value before implementing a complex latent-belief controller. This turns the remaining belief-state solver from an open-ended optimization task into a bounded marginal-value check.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Before building a complex nonrectangular belief-state evaluator, construct a finite library of valid horizon-aware policies, solve its primal maximin/dual least-favorable-prior game, and compare the game value to a map-specific universal upper bound. Use the dual support to identify which transfer environments are actually binding at that horizon.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Refined T=100/T=200 policy games equalized correct/inverted power with flat slack and left only ~0.006/~0.055 percentage-point gaps to the inverted-map upper bound. The library-relative least-favorable prior shifted from nearly pure inverted toward a small correct component as horizon grew.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Randomized component selection must be fixed before outcomes. The finite-game saddle is library-relative; the upper-bound gap, not the LP alone, limits claims about the full policy space.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Quantify the maximum possible gain from a more complex latent-map belief controller before implementing it: upper bound by the individually hardest map optimum and subtract the best certified simple/library robust value. Skip or deprioritize belief-state complexity when the residual headroom is below the evaluation resolution/MDE.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Headroom after the refined library saddle was only ~0.0061 pp at T=100 and ~0.0548 pp at T=200 in the current setup.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Only valid when the chosen map-specific optimum is a genuine upper bound for the same policy class/objective and is computed accurately enough; discretization error can dominate tiny gaps.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected: 'the least-favorable environment is horizon invariant.' In the finite policy-game dual, support moved from pure inverted at T=50 to a correct+inverted mixture by T=100/T=200.

Rejected: 'a full belief-state nonrectangular controller is automatically worth implementing once fixed-latent ambiguity is recognized.' The universal upper-bound gap shows at most ~0.006 pp T=100 and ~0.055 pp T=200 improvement remains in this setup before accounting for numerical error.

Narrowed: 'flat transfer uncertainty is an important worst-case scenario because it lies between correct and inverted pointwise.' It received zero least-favorable mass in the refined T=100/T=200 finite games and was slack at the saddle; intermediate parameter values need not be decision-theoretically binding.

Narrowed: 'randomized robust testing is just averaging reported power.' Ex-ante independent randomization is a legitimate decision rule, but outcome-adaptive policy selection is not free and deterministic wealth-mixtures have different crossing behavior from randomized rule mixtures.

frontier.action: Check whether a deterministic single-process approximation can match the refined randomized-library saddle without external randomization, for example by optimizing a history/wealth-dependent affine policy directly against the two binding correct/inverted maps. Preserve the same anytime-valid factor constraint.

Because belief-learning headroom is now numerically tiny in the current three-map setup, add a harmful/non-improving q<=.5 map and explicit asymmetric harmful-commit/unresolved costs before spending substantial compute on a full belief-state solver. Recompute least-favorable support under those deployment-relevant losses.
Stress misspecified map support and one-switch latent environments to identify when the fixed-latent advantage disappears and partially rectangular ambiguity is justified.
Generalize the pre-outcome filtration provenance gate to actual evaluator traces and then resume reused-development PACE path selection/multiplicity work.

frontier.exact_next_action: Add a harmful/non-improving fixed latent map and an asymmetric harmful-commit versus unresolved loss, then solve the finite policy-game primal/dual again. Determine whether the least-favorable support and preferred robustness objective change enough to dominate the tiny remaining benefit of a full latent-belief controller.
